idea: In y=a(x−h)2+k, the vertex is (h,k) and the extreme value is k. The vertex sits halfway between any two inputs with equal outputs, including the two zeros, so h=2r+s​ for y=a(x−r)(x−s).
trap: Reading the vertex of a(x+3)2 as x=3; the sign flips.
desmos: Desmos marks the vertex of a graph you can type in. When a coefficient is unknown, use symmetry to find h first; then one more fact pins down the rest.

items.stem: The function f(x)=x2+14x+c, where c is a constant, has a minimum value of −7. What is the value of c?
items.explain: The minimum occurs at x=−214​=−7, where f=49−98+c=c−49. Setting c−49=−7 gives c=42.

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x)=a(x+3)(x−7), where a is a constant. The maximum value of f is 25. What is the value of f(7)?
items.explain: The vertex is halfway between the zeros −3 and 7, at x=2. So f(2)=a(5)(−5)=−25a=25, which gives a=−1. Then f(7)=−1(10)(0)=0.

items.stem: The height, in feet, of a ball t seconds after it is thrown is h(t)=−16t2+bt+7, where b is a constant. The ball is at the same height at t=1 and at t=5. What is the maximum height, in feet, that the ball reaches?
items.explain: Equal heights put the vertex halfway between the two times, at t=3. The vertex of −16t2+bt+7 is at t=32b​, so b=96. The maximum is h(3)=−16(3)2+96(3)+7=151.
